question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{coth}^{2}⁡x{sinh}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities corresponding to the trigonometric identities 

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{coth}^{2}⁡x{sinh}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sech}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {sinh}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-\operatorname{sinh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{0}-{e}^{-0}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-{3}^{-1}}{2}-\frac{1-1}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{8}{3})}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
